problem: Which value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\frac{3x-1}{{x}^{2}}=\frac{2}{x}-\frac{x-3}{{x}^{2}}?$

feedback.worked_solution:
We note that $y=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $4y,\,{y}^{2},$ and $2{y}^{2}.$ First, we find the denominators' least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$). We have that

$$
\text{LCM}(4y,{y}^{2},2{y}^{2})=4{y}^{2}.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $4{y}^{2},$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y+2}{{y}^{2}}-\frac{5}{4y} & =\frac{3}{2{y}^{2}} \\ 4{y}^{2}(\frac{y+2}{{y}^{2}}-\frac{5}{4y}) & =4{y}^{2}(\frac{3}{2{y}^{2}}) \\ 4{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{y+2}{{y}^{2}}-4{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{4y} & =4{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2{y}^{2}} \\ 4\cdot {y}^{2}\cdot \frac{y+2}{{y}^{2}}-4y\cdot y\cdot \frac{5}{4y} & =2\cdot 2{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2{y}^{2}} \\ 4\cdot \cancel{{y}^{2}}\cdot \frac{y+2}{\cancel{{y}^{2}}}-\cancel{4y}\cdot y\cdot \frac{5}{\cancel{4y}} & =2\cdot \cancel{2{y}^{2}}\cdot \frac{3}{\cancel{2{y}^{2}}} \\ 4(y+2)-y\cdot 5 & =2\cdot 3\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $y,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(y+2)-y\cdot 5 & =2\cdot 3 \\ 4y+8-5y & =6 \\ -y+8 & =6 \\ -y & =-2 \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $y=0$ as a solution. But since $y=2\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $y=2.$
